title: Challenge - Clone my game!
author: eyesolatedgames
selftext:
Recently, I've seen a lot of posts across all social media channels of Indie Developers in active fear over their game getting cloned by someone using AI within a week. Mostly, I replay with "simple idea, simple clone" or insinuate that they did something wrong if they spent months/years developing something that can be cloned in that timeframe.

I strongly believe that AI can do quite a few things, but I believe that my game is "immune" to simple cloning. It's a puzzle game with relatively straightforward mechanics, but the beauty is in the detail.

So I challenge everyone to actually produce a good clone of my game to prove me wrong. There's trailers and a Demo as well as a few Screenshots and other information. The game title is **Cubic Color Confusion**. You can find information on Steam, Itch, Twitter/X.

I am really interested on what people can put together. The full game releases on November 10th, with 100 Levels and the Steam Workshop integrated Level Editor.

Challenge accepted?

replies.author: eyesolatedgames
replies.body:
Too bad. Why though?

Wouldn't you agree that the whole fearmongering propaganda currently going around is totally blown out of proportion?

A working prototype / tech demo and a real game are two very different things.

comments.author: Kosh_Ascadian
comments.body:
Why would you think that game is not cloneable?

Seems pretty basic and easy to do. Like what about this is immune?

replies.author: eyesolatedgames
replies.body:
The campaign features 100 levels. Puzzle design can't be cloned. Sure, you can probably copy the Levels shown in the Demo, but can AI extrapolate interesting Levels beyond what is available?

What about the Level Editor? There's a screenshot and a bit of descriptions scattered around, but even then I'm pretty confident that the UX won't be nearly the same. In regards to UX, that goes for the entire game.

But hey, what do I know, maybe pointing a competent AI agent towards the Steam site and doing "create this" is actually enough and the fear is warranted.

replies.author: Kosh_Ascadian
replies.body:
I don't buy it.

But I'm also in no way ever going to spend 3-4 full development days doing unethical bs to prove a random person online wrong, so I quess that's that.

replies.author: eyesolatedgames
replies.body:
That's fine. I still think the mechanics are probably easy to copy, but the content? Design philosophy behind all that? No way.

It's easy to copy "Clean up the Toy Store" or "Find the needle in the Haystack" and things like that, because it's mostly systems-driven. Basically, the Idea/Core Mechanic IS the game, there's not a lot of content you have to "manually" create after the fact.

replies.author: DojiRun
replies.body: how is it unethical if they are literally challenging you to try it?

replies.author: Kosh_Ascadian
replies.body:
How do I even know its the same guy?

I also think it'd be a pretty big waste of resources which achieves nothing of value and thus unethical. By default.

Etc. Various reasons made my write that one word in that sentence... who cares really. That one word wasnt the point.

replies.author: DojiRun
replies.body: I mean, look at his profile, and the steam page it is obviously the same guy. also it is relevant because this is a huge claim from the anti crowd right now. nothing wrong with the challenge.

replies.author: eyesolatedgames
replies.body:
Yeah it's me (@eyesolated1 on X/Twitter). And that's the whole point of the challenge - the Anti-AI movement and the fearmongering on all socials at the moment.

My point is, you only have to fear an AI clone if your game isn't really complex and/or doesn't a lot of "human-only" stuff in it (like level design or something not obviously visible by playing a demo or watching someone "build in public").

replies.author: supimjay
replies.body:
I mean I kind of agree this is a pointless challenge. The anti-ai crowd doesn’t use ai so they aren’t going to be successful or have the means set up to do it. The pro ai crowd has no reason to try to prove that ai can be used in ways that contribute to fear mongering.

I don’t think there’s anything unethical about the challenge though lol, if anything it seems like you are just trying to get people to look up your game!

replies.author: Kosh_Ascadian
replies.body: What the main point was and what is wrong with the challenge is: Theres 0 incentive here to do any of this. It's days of work to prove some rando online wrong.

replies.author: eyesolatedgames
replies.body: True - can't give any incentives, except to prove me wrong.

replies.author: JordanRunsForFun
replies.body:
The 100 levels are safe-ish if they can't be easily mined from the data, otherwise they are easily stolen. A level editor is easy for Claude, in fact a good game dev builds it first for themselves and second for users. What can protect you are algorithms and complexity. Algorithms are often what make a game good (see BlockBlast) and unless they are simplistic or deterministic they can't be copied (unless we are talking about decompiling, but that's a whole step darker than general game cloning). 

But I think more than anything - just having a name and a reputation and doing your thing first is the most important thing.

replies.author: eyesolatedgames
replies.body:
Well the demo obviously(?) doesn't ship with all 100 levels in the binaries, apart from that you're right of course. You are also right on the level editor, i DID build it for myself and polished it to be ready for the players.

For this type of game, there's no real algorithm that could be protected. The only complexity is the system/mechanic interaction.

The point is that there is stuff in games (like manually crafted puzzle levels) that can't be cloned just with access to the demo (or like some people claim, "building in public"). It's just fearmongering, insecurity and clickbait.

comments.author: FinsAssociate
comments.body: People clone games that look marketable

replies.author: eyesolatedgames
replies.body: For what I've seen, people clone games that are so insanely simple gameplay-wise that even without AI, a clone wouldn't take a lot of time - eg. sorting games, simple incremental games. Things where "Design" is mostly irrelevant and everything comes from the underlying systems and presentation of said systems.

comments.author: AccomplishedArea6577
comments.body: Easy to do for anyone who wanted to.  Download the game. Decompile and decrypt it. Recompile with a new name and get ai to change up the lightning or something. People that clone games literally clone then. They don't prompt ai to remake it. They decompile the games code modify it then recompile as a new game.

replies.author: eyesolatedgames
replies.body: And then you have a copy of a demo version, with 80% of the content missing. Content that AI can't easily create.
